chosen.title: Every Kind of Love Is a Mix of 3 Ingredients (v2, illustrated)
chosen.angle: Sternberg's triangle as a recipe: three ingredients (intimacy, passion, commitment); every mix gives a different kind of love. Frame as a quick self-check, not a lecture.
chosen.hook: Every kind of love is a mix of just three ingredients.

claims.claim: Robert Sternberg published 'A Triangular Theory of Love' in Psychological Review in 1986 (vol. 93, pp. 119-135).
The three components are intimacy, passion, and decision/commitment.
Intimacy = closeness, connectedness, bondedness; passion = drives behind attraction, romance, arousal; commitment = the decision to love and to maintain that love.
The theory yields eight types: nonlove, liking, infatuation, empty, romantic, companionate, fatuous, consummate.
Companionate = intimacy + commitment, no passion (e.g. deep friendships, long marriages where the heat has faded).
